symptom: `targeting users xpath [System.UserRoles = '[%UserRole_Manager%]']` with no Manager user role passed `check -p --references` and exec; mx check reported CE1613 "The selected user role 'Manager' no longer exists." — and, with that CE1613 in the app, no CE0161 anywhere, hiding four invalid targeting constraints during #1711's measurement. The same token in a retrieve, a list view's database source and an access rule is CE1613 at each (11.15.0), and the name is case-sensitive: '[%UserRole_user%]' is CE1613 where '[%UserRole_User%]' is clean
cause: No validator read the name inside an XPath token: the member walks treat a quoted token as a literal, and the reference pass resolves qualified names, which a token is not
file: `mdl/executor/validate_user_role_tokens.go` (new: validateUserRoleTokens, walkXPathConstraints, userRoleNames), wired after validateEnumValueRefs in `mdl/executor/validate.go`
insight: One reflective walk with a type switch on the nodes that HOLD an XPath (RetrieveStmt.Where via expressionToXPath, DataSourceV3.Where, GrantEntityAccessStmt.XPathConstraint, WorkflowTargetingNode.XPath, SetActivityPropertyOp targeting_xpath, NavSyncDef.Constraint) covers every slot wherever it nests — alter page, alter workflow, navigation — without a per-statement collector; scanning every string instead would flag a log message that mentions a token. A node held by value has to be routed through its address or the struct walk recurses into itself. mx check validates the role name but not every enum: a non-interrupting timer's Recurrence.IntervalType 'Bogus' passed mx check (#1716), so 'mx check accepted it' proves a value only where a bogus control fails
fix: Collect the role names from GetProjectSecurity plus the script's create user role statements; report each unknown token per statement as CE1613 with the role list, and the right spelling when only the case differs. Excluded flows warn. No project or no security document: silent
